title: Refinish the Old Hardwood or Cover It With Vinyl Plank? The Smarter Choice for Sammamish Homes
meta: In most Sammamish homes, refinishing the oak at $3.99 per sq ft beats covering it with vinyl plank on cost and resale. Wills Flooring lists the exceptions.
keywords: refinish hardwood or install vinyl plank, cover hardwood floors with vinyl plank, refinish vs replace hardwood with LVP, is it worth refinishing old hardwood, hardwood floor refinishing Sammamish WA

blocks.lead: If the hardwood is sound, refinish it. A natural sand and finish is $3.99 per sq ft all-in, while covering the same floor with vinyl plank is $2.50 per sq ft in labor before you buy a single plank, and it hides the one feature Sammamish buyers pay most for.
blocks.detail: Vinyl plank wins in a few specific cases: the wood is too thin or too damaged to sand, water is a recurring problem, or you need one waterproof surface across a whole open plan with kids and dogs. Wills Flooring does both jobs, so we can tell you which one your floor actually needs.

blocks.html: Most of the plateau was built between 1990 and 2010, and most of those houses in Pine Lake, Klahanie, Trossachs and Sahalee came with red oak on the main floor. Twenty-five years, two dogs and three kids later, the oak is scratched and orange, and vinyl plank ads make covering it look like the modern, waterproof fix. The question comes to us a couple of times a week: is it smarter to sand the oak we have or lay vinyl plank over it? The answer is usually the oak, and the reasons are about money, resale and what happens under a floating floor. The exceptions are real, though, and we cover them too.

blocks.text: What you gain and what you give up with each

items.title: Refinish: you keep the asset
items.text: Real oak on a Sammamish main floor is a line item in the listing and something buyers check with their shoes. A refinished floor can be recoated for decades. The wood stays at its original height, so doors, stairs and transitions all still work.

items.title: Refinish: you live with wood
items.text: Oak scratches, dents and marks under standing water. A natural finish shows the red tone of red oak unless you stain it. Sanding is three to five days of noise and the family usually stays elsewhere.

items.title: Vinyl plank: waterproof and quiet to install
items.text: Spills, wet dogs and dropped water bowls do nothing to it. No sanding dust, one or two days, and you can pick any color or wide-plank look without stain.

items.title: Vinyl plank: you bury the oak
items.text: The floor rises by the plank thickness, so doors get trimmed and stair noses change. Any moisture already in the oak is trapped. And a buyer who lifts a vent cover and sees hardwood underneath asks why it was covered, not how nice the vinyl is.

blocks.text: When covering the hardwood is actually the smarter call

a.title: Sand the oak when
items: At least 3/32 in of wood remains above the tongue
Damage is scratches, gray finish, sun fade and surface pet stains
You want the best resale story on the plateau
You can be out of the house for three to five days

b.title: Cover or replace when
items: The oak is cupped or black from a long-term leak and boards are soft
It has been sanded three or more times and is too thin to go again
You need one waterproof floor through kitchen, mudroom and family room
Only part of the floor is oak and you want one surface everywhere

blocks.html: One more honest case: a badly damaged oak floor sometimes belongs neither under vinyl nor under a sander. If boards are soft or the subfloor moves, the right fix is to remove the oak and install new flooring on a repaired subfloor, whether that is vinyl plank or new hardwood. Covering a failing floor just hides the problem until it comes through the seams.

rules.p: Cupped, black or soft oak should come out, and the subfloor should be checked, before any new floor goes down. Vinyl plank over a failing floor traps the problem. We will price removal plus new flooring at the estimate.

rules.h: Either works; vinyl plank is defensible
rules.p: Your oak is sound, but you want waterproof and you are staying. A refinish with a durable satin finish will hold up, and vinyl plank is a fair choice if you value zero water worry over keeping the wood. We would show you both prices.

Sound hardwood is the strongest resale feature on a Sammamish main floor. A natural refinish at $3.99 per sq ft is usually cheaper than a quality vinyl plank floor and it is what the next buyer wants to see.

default.p: Sound oak with surface wear is the ideal refinish candidate. Sanding costs less than covering it with a quality plank and keeps the floor at its original height. Book a free estimate and we will confirm the wood thickness.

blocks.text: Mistakes we see on the plateau

items.html: Comparing the $2.50 labor rate to the $3.99 refinish rate. One is labor only; the other includes the finish. Add the plank, the stair noses, the transitions and the door trimming before deciding which is cheaper.
Covering oak because it is orange. The color is the finish and the species, not damage. A stain at $6.50 per sq ft gives you the light or greige look that vinyl plank imitates, on real wood.

Floating plank over a floor that is not flat. Old oak with a hump at a joist or a dip at the fireplace will telegraph through vinyl and break the click joints. Flattening it costs money the ads never mention.
Ignoring the HOA and the neighbors. In Klahanie and Trossachs, resale is set by comparables. If every other house on the street shows hardwood, covered oak reads as a downgrade.
Skipping the recoat option. If the finish is dull but not worn through, a $1.99 screen-and-recoat resets it for a fraction of either alternative. Ask before you assume sanding or covering.

items: Pull a floor vent and measure the wood above the tongue. Under 3/32 in changes the answer.
Get a moisture reading on any black or cupped area before anyone quotes either option.
Ask for two written prices on the same measured square footage: refinish, and vinyl plank installed with material.
Check three recent sales on your street and note which ones showed hardwood.
Decide who is living in the house during the work. Refinishing means three to five days out; plank means one or two days of noise.
If you choose vinyl plank, insist on a plank with a 20 mil or thicker wear layer, or you will be doing this again.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to refinish hardwood or install vinyl plank over it?
faq.a: Usually refinishing. A natural sand and finish is $3.99 per sq ft all-in. Vinyl plank is $2.50 per sq ft in labor plus the plank itself, trim and transitions, and a quality plank pushes the total to or above the refinish. On 1,200 sq ft, the refinish is $4,788 with finish included.

faq.q: Does covering hardwood with vinyl plank hurt resale in Sammamish?
faq.a: In most plateau neighborhoods, yes. Buyers expect hardwood on the main floor of a Pine Lake or Klahanie home and check for it. Covered oak reads as a shortcut. Refinished oak, natural or stained, is the stronger listing and photographs better.

faq.q: Can vinyl plank be installed directly over hardwood?
faq.a: Yes, if the hardwood is flat, dry and firmly fastened. Cupped or loose boards must be fixed first, and the added height means trimming doors and changing stair noses. Any moisture in the oak is sealed in, so a moisture reading is required before we would do it.

faq.q: How do I know if my hardwood is too thin to refinish?
faq.a: Lift a floor vent or a closet threshold and measure from the top of the board to the tongue. About 3/32 in or more means another full sanding is safe. Most 1990s Sammamish builder oak has been sanded once or never, so it almost always has room.

faq.q: Can I get the gray or light modern look without vinyl plank?
faq.a: Yes. Red oak can be sanded and stained to a light, cool or greige tone at $6.50 per sq ft with finish included. It will not look identical to a whitewashed vinyl plank because it is real grain, but it gives the modern look buyers want while keeping the hardwood.

faq.q: How long does each option take?
faq.a: A natural refinish on a 1,200 sq ft main floor is three to four days, plus a day if stained, and the family usually stays out during sanding and finishing. Vinyl plank over the same area is one to two days with no dust, plus door trimming and transitions.
